0.reason: a deliberate trade the earlier review asked for: the check fires only on a label sentence, so mid-paragraph prose no longer floods audit-doc; the 162 mid-paragraph mentions are prose, not labels

findings.text: non-blocking: the check now fires only where a paragraph's visible text begins with the write-paths label, so a section whose only write-paths mention sits mid-paragraph in a form neither reader parses is no longer reported. Measured 162 such sections over docs/plans and docs/evidence at fab91223 (corpus-count.log), none of which warn; if one of them states its fence in prose, the audit stays silent while the batch reader refuses the dispatch. The narrowing is the review's request and is the right trade, but the silent population is worth knowing about.

non-blocking: the section identity is read from the raw h2 id attribute, while _plan_html.section_prose yields section_record_id's derived identity (casefolded, with a dotted number normalised, so s5.1 becomes s5-1); a plan whose heading id is spelled differently from its section record would be compared against a different key than the one the parseable set holds. No such id exists in the corpus today (3119 h2 ids surveyed, 0 dotted or uppercase), so the mismatch is latent rather than current, and using section_record_id would remove it.

non-blocking: the head arm at 344fc562 runs only this test file and tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py, so the changed audit_html is not exercised by tests/test_doccheck.py at the head; the wide arm that includes test_doccheck.py ran at c3ca399f, before this change. The risk is low because the new module was exercised over 2331 corpus documents by the count run without error, but the repository's own doccheck tests have not seen the new code.
